newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Electronics help Taiwan stocks to 7-yr high close.
newsitem.headline: Electronics help Taiwan stocks to 7-yr high close.

text.p: Taiwan share prices pushed to yet another seven-year high close on Monday, as strong performances by electronics and construction shares helped the index to its fourth consecutive daily gain, brokers said.
The weighted index surged as high as 9,370.41 points, a seven-year intraday high, and ended at 9,322.84, a gain of 64.21 points or 0.69 percent.
Monday's close surpassed an April 30, 1990, finish of 9,292.37 points. The index has not closed lower since 9,665.50 finish on April 28, 1990.
Turnover was a heavy T$179.8 billion.
The index rose despite expectations of tightening liquidity after the central bank announced it would issue T$11 billion in three-month negotiable certificates of deposit later on Monday.

"Sentiment surely continues to be bullish as the most bearish news is the central bank's NCD issue, considered only as a mild move to cool the red-hot stock market," said HSBC James Capel research chief Alex Chen.
Electronics continued to attract heavy buying, rising 2.27 percent on expected sound June sales, which must be reported by July 10.
Microchip maker United Microelectronics surged T$4 to T$124.5 while rival Winbond was up the daily seven percent limit, or T$3.5, to T$58.5.

Formosa Plastics group member Nan Ya Plastics rose T$1.5 to T$85.5 after saying its 56 percent-owned Nan Ya Technology would pour more than T$100 billion over five years into three new wafer fabrication plants in northern Taiwan.
The announcement was the fifth involving major wafermaking plants in three months, following huge projects by Taiwan's number one and two chipmakers, Taiwan Semiconductor and United Microelectronics.
